children: Shares of Glass Wall Systems (India) made a positive debut on the stock exchanges on Wednesday, rising 6.6 per cent over the IPO price to open at Rs 194 apiece on the NSE.

The stock was issued at Rs 182, while it listed at Rs 190.10 on the BSE, marking a 4.5 per cent premium. The debut came after the company’s Rs 427.89 crore initial public offering (IPO) received overwhelming demand during its September 8-10 subscription window.

The issue was subscribed 81.65 times overall, with the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion receiving 167.93 times subscription. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 79.71 times, while the retail portion saw 33.18 times subscription. Investors bid for 134.37 crore shares against 1.64 crore shares on offer.

Ahead of the listing, the stock was commanding a grey-market premium of around Rs 41, implying an indicative price of Rs 223. The actual NSE debut, however, was considerably below that unofficial indication.
Glass Wall Systems had fixed its IPO price band at Rs 172-182 per share and raised Rs 128.36 crore from anchor investors before the issue opened.

The anchor allocation comprised 70.53 lakh shares at Rs 182 apiece and included investments from HDFC Mutual Fund, Bank of India Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance Company, Abakkus Growth Fund, Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), PineBridge India Equity Fund and other institutional investors.

The IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 60 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 2.02 crore shares by promoters Jawahar Hariram Hemrajani and Eshan Jawahar Hemrajani, along with investor shareholder India Business Excellence Fund IIA. The OFS accounted for the bulk of the issue, at around Rs 368 crore.

Of the fresh capital, Rs 50 crore is earmarked for setting up a glass-processing facility at the company’s Vile Bhagad plant in Maharashtra as part of its backward-integration plans. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2002, Glass Wall Systems provides façade and fenestration solutions, covering design, engineering, manufacturing, supply and installation. Its operations span the domestic market as well as overseas markets including the US and Australia.
The company manufactures customised façade systems and caters to projects requiring architectural and building-envelope solutions.

The listing gives the company access to public-market capital at a time when its IPO attracted substantial institutional and retail demand. The stock’s opening premium, however, was well below the premium indicated by the grey market ahead of its debut.
